name: Nairobi
tagline: Safari Capital with Year-Round Spring Weather and a Booming Tech Scene
description: Nairobi is East Africa's most dynamic city, offering FIRE retirees a unique combination of urban sophistication, wildlife literally at the city's edge, and a surprisingly strong expat infrastructure. The climate at 5,500 feet elevation is perpetual spring. English is an official language and widely spoken. Private healthcare is solid and affordable, the food scene blends Kenyan, Indian, and international cuisines, and Nairobi National Park means you can watch lions with the city skyline as a backdrop. Kenya's growing tech hub, dubbed Silicon Savannah, gives the city a forward-looking energy.

quickFacts.visa: eVisa required for US citizens (90 days, renewable). No dedicated retirement visa. Residence permits available through investment ($100K+) or as a person of independent means with sufficient passive income.
quickFacts.safetyRating: Moderate – exercise caution, especially at night; secure compounds recommended
quickFacts.climate: Subtropical highland with mild temperatures year-round

housing.description: Secure but basic apartment in a gated Kilimani or Lavington block — the safety premium is non-negotiable

dining.description: Local nyama-choma/Indian joints and kibandas a few times a week

healthcare.description: Basic local private cover for a 45–55 early retiree, inpatient-focused

transportation.description: Bolt/Uber for everyday trips — safer than self-driving

1M.lifestyle: A secure, gated apartment in Kilimani or Lavington — the safety premium is non-negotiable in Nairobi, so the compound guard and walls come standard. Most meals are cooked from cheap, excellent local produce, with nyama-choma and Indian spots for eating out a few times a week. Getting around leans on Bolt and Uber rather than self-driving, which is safer and simpler in the traffic. Cover is a real but basic local private plan, inpatient-focused. A neighborhood gym and the odd cinema or bar fill the discretionary slack, and the highland climate means no heating or cooling bills.

2M.lifestyle: An upscale furnished apartment in buzzy Westlands or leafy Kilimani, dining out several evenings a week including mid-range restaurants. Comprehensive local insurance (Jubilee, AAR, or Britam) now covers outpatient visits too, not just hospital stays. Transport leans on ride-hail heavily, or a modest small car. A mid-range gym plus nightlife and weekend outings keep things social — unstressed but not lavish.

3M.lifestyle: A serviced flat in a prime area like Westlands, Riverside, Kilimani, or Lavington, where security, housekeeping, and backup power are bundled into the rent. Eating out is frequent and good, healthcare is a strong private plan with high limits and medical-evacuation cover, and travel happens most months — a Maasai Mara safari lodge or a Diani-coast weekend. Transport is frictionless: unlimited Bolt/Uber plus a hired driver when wanted, or a comfortable owned car.

5M.lifestyle: Upper-crust living — a furnished Runda or Karen cottage, or a Riverside penthouse, kept by a part-time housekeeper and a part-time driver. Dining out is almost daily, including Nairobi's top restaurants and hotel venues, healthcare is a genuine top-tier international plan, and a private-club membership comes with it. A standalone house means a generator, borehole, security, and pool upkeep, all handled. Safari, coast, and regional travel are routine — unmistakably affluent.

10M.lifestyle: Top-of-market Nairobi — a luxury furnished house in Karen or Runda, run by full-time staff: a live-in housekeeper/cook, a driver, and day-and-night guarding. Dining ranges from top hotel restaurants to private-chef nights, and international concierge cover gives full global access with evacuation. A large house runs on full power with backup generator, borehole, pool, and security, and the discretionary budget funds clubs, first-class travel, golf, and sailing. This is Nairobi at its most opulent — a leafy prime-suburb estate, resident staff, and the Mara and coast on call.
